quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a surface with good grip, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a surface with good grip, you can keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will stay under control if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Block side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, give clear views to the sides, fasten securely, allow air to prevent fogging, and fit eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Good because it blocks the wind.
Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to cars or trucks. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could turn into your lane.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of a small vehicle like a motorcycle. Other drivers may not be able to accurately judge your speed and location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road is divided ahead.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could make the bike tip over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could make the bike tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Instead, use the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Look ahead at your path.
Be ready to avoid a hazard.
Turn off your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your headlight during the day.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Squeezing the front brake hard or slamming the rear brake:

options.text: Can cause the brakes to lock.
Is the best way to stop in an emergency.
Is the best way to slow down on wet streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause the brakes to lock.
questions.explanation: Squeezing the front brake hard or slamming the rear brake can lock the brakes. This causes control problems.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.

options.text: More noticeable than
Just as noticeable as
Not as noticeable as

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as visible as a larger vehicle's brake light, especially when the taillight is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other drivers you are riding near them.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping suddenly where they don't expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping suddenly where they don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Use your brake light to communicate with other drivers. It is very important to flash your brake light before making a sharp turn off a high-speed road. Flash your brake light whenever you slow down where other drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: Road surface is about to change
Traffic around you
Conditions that stay the same as you get closer

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that stay the same as you get closer
questions.explanation: Look ahead for problems on the road. Make a plan to stay safe.

questions.question: Why does a motorcycle rider have an advantage over a car driver when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: A motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
A motorcycle can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
Motorcycles stop faster than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
questions.explanation: When parked cars are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane. This helps you avoid open doors, people getting out, or people stepping between cars. Only do this if no traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: When there is at least eight feet of clear road on the right.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on flat grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is at least eight feet of clear road on the right.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles are entering the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when safe.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid sudden moves. Quick moves can cause a skid.
Ride on the shoulder to stay away from traffic.
Use only the rear brake. The front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves. Quick moves can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, change gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: What does it feel like if your front tire goes flat?

options.text: Steering feels heavy
Steering feels loose
Steering feels soft

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering feels heavy
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind. A windshield does not. A windshield alone is not enough protection for your eyes.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ maintenance.

options.text: Less often
The same amount
More often

questions.correctAnswerText: More often
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs more frequent maintenance than a car. Check your bike before riding in traffic or on the highway.

questions.question: How should a passenger hold on?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Never hold onto the rider.
Do not lean into any turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. If there are handholds, they can use those instead.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk is at intersections. The biggest danger is when a car turns left in front of a motorcycle.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit upright so your arms can control the motorcycle. Your arms should not hold up your body or support your weight.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Wear half-fingered gloves.
Wear full-fingered gloves.
Not wear gloves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of durable material. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.

questions.question: Stopping in a turn can be difficult because:

options.text: There is decreased traction available for stopping while the bike is leaning.
The rider is usually focused on the turn and not on the braking.
The brake controls do not work in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is decreased traction available for stopping while the bike is leaning.
questions.explanation: While turning, your motorcycle is leaning. Some traction is used for the turn, so less is available for braking. You can brake while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely enough to allow the wind to catch the fabric.
Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
Be tight enough to prevent you from moving freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind. They should still be loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Use gentle pressure.
